pages.text: Cables carry power and fluids from one machine to another, so your machines no longer need to touch. To move items, use a drone with a $(l:drone_systems/modules)Transport Module$(/l) instead.$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy Conduit$(/l)$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/energy_conduit)Advanced Energy Conduit$(/l)$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/energy_conduit)Elite Energy Conduit$(/l)

There are three kinds of cable. All are glass tubes, and the lit sleeves near their ends tell them apart:$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy Conduit$(/l): FE, cyan$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipe$(/l): gases: biogas, methane, Steam, green$(br)$(li)$(l:cables/liquid_pipe)Liquid Pipe$(/l): liquids: water, lava, coolants, acid, blue
pages.title: Kinds and tiers

pages.text: Each kind comes in $(l)three tiers$(): Basic, Advanced and Elite. The band on the sleeve shows the tier: grey, $(l)gold$() or $(l)violet$(). You can see when something goes through a cable.
$(li)A cable $(l)connects by itself$() to cables of the same kind.$(br)$(li)It also connects to any block that takes what it carries, from CyberFarm or any other mod.
pages.title: Placing cables

pages.text: $(li)Machines built with $(l:basics/cyber_frame)Cyber Frames$(/l) take cables, pipes and hoppers on $(l)any of their frames$(), not only on the machine block.$(br)$(li)Different kinds never connect to each other, so they can run side by side.$(br)$(li)All tiers of one kind join into one network.
$(li)A network can be up to $(l)1,024$() cables long.$(br)$(li)Cables $(l)store nothing$(): what comes in goes straight to the blocks at the other end.
Generators and machines push what they make into the cables by themselves. Batteries, tanks and other storage do not.
pages.title: Pulling out of a block

pages.text: To take something $(l)out$() of a storage block, $(l)right-click the cable's arm$() that touches it. A lit band wraps that end, and the cable now $(l)pulls$() from that block every tick, up to its tier's rate. Right-click the arm again to stop.

The network never sends anything back into a block it pulls from, so a pulling arm is a one-way exit. Use it to empty a $(l:cables/fluid_tanks)Liquid Tank or Gas Tank$(/l) or a battery of another mod.

The $(l)rate$() is the most that can enter the network per tick $(l)from each source$(): each generator or machine pushing in, or each block a cable pulls from. The cable touching the source sets it.$(br)$(li)$(l)Energy Conduit$(): 2,000 FE/t, 16,000 FE/t, 128,000 FE/t
pages.title: Numbers

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Gas Pipe$(): 1,000 mB/t, 4,000 mB/t, 16,000 mB/t$(br)$(li)$(l)Liquid Pipe$(): 1,000 mB/t, 4,000 mB/t, 16,000 mB/t$(br)Because the rate depends only on the cable at the source, you can mix tiers in one network: put a better cable right where a big producer connects. As a guide:

$(li)$(l)Basic$() carries all the gas power and a Small Steam Turbine (2,000 FE/t).$(br)$(li)$(l)Advanced$() carries a Medium Steam Turbine (9,600 FE/t) or the steam of a Large reactor (up to 2,000 mB/t).
$(li)$(l)Elite$() carries a Large Steam Turbine (40,000 FE/t) and joins several turbines into one line.$(br)These numbers sit between Immersive Engineering's wires and Mekanism's cables.
$(li)6 cables around two gold ingots and a Basic Circuit make $(l)8 Advanced$() cables.$(br)$(li)6 Advanced cables around two diamonds and an Advanced Circuit make $(l)8 Elite$() cables.
pages.title: Upgrading

pages.text: To upgrade a line already in place, use the $(l:cables/cable_swapper)Cable Swapper$(/l): one right-click swaps the whole line for the next tier.$(br2)Where a cable can't go, $(l:cables/dish_transmission)Dish Transmission$(/l) sends FE through the air.
